paper_metadata.title: Solving the Product Breakdown Structure Problem with constrained QAOA

summary: The paper proposes a constrained-QAOA approach for the Product Breakdown Structure (PBS) problem that prepares a uniform superposition of feasible solutions using M·N qubits and achieves circuit complexity O(p·M^2·N) gates and O(p·M·N) depth. Simulator experiments (3-layer QAOA) show probability amplification for near-optimal solutions and demonstrate a search-space reduction of up to 46 orders of magnitude at M=20 compared with unconstrained QUBO formulations. Additional simulations up to 24 qubits suggest reduced barren-plateau effects via gradient-variance analysis.

experiments.description: Constrained QAOA for the Product Breakdown Structure (PBS) problem, benchmarked on multiple randomly generated PBS tree instances with varying numbers of sites and tree structures, using Qrisp simulator.

algorithm.variant: constrained QAOA with constraint-specific state preparation and constrained mixer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed-depth benchmark with depth 3; additional sweep over 0 to 4 layers in figures
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Trotterized Quantum Annealing (TQA) parameter initialization protocol; initial state set to uniform superposition over feasible solutions

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each part is encoded as a one-hot QuantumVariable of N qubits; M parts use M·N qubits total
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize C = sum_{(r,s) in phi} c^r_{f(r),f(s)} subject to f(r) != f(s) for all (r,s) in {x} ∪ pred(x)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraints are enforced directly in the state preparation and mixer (feasible-subspace-preserving constrained mixer), not via penalty terms in the implemented QAOA; paper also discusses QUBO penalty formulation as a contrast

problem_instance.description: Product Breakdown Structure (PBS) assignment problem on rooted directed tree instances; benchmark instances are randomly generated tree graphs and examples from prior PBS benchmark set
problem_instance.dataset_name: PBS benchmark instances / randomly generated tree graphs

dataset_specification.description: Tree graphs with maximum degree N = floor(M/2) for scaling study; example instances include phi={(1,0),(2,0),(3,0)} and phi={(1,0),(2,0),(3,1)} with N in {4,5,6}

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Random tree generation for scaling study; no additional preprocessing reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulator-based benchmarking; aggregated probabilities of measuring feasible solutions and success probability P0.1 over varying QAOA layers; 30 random graphs per M for scaling figure; 100 samples for gradient-variance study in Appendix B

quantum_resources.mixer_depth: Mixer includes state-preparation conjugation and is dominated by state preparation complexity O(M·N); the MCP tagging subroutine itself has depth O(log N)

hardware.device_name: Qrisp simulator running on Apple M2 MacBook Pro

noise_model.noise_model: noiseless simulation; no noise model reported

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Qrisp compiler; no specific backend target reported
implementation_details.classical_solver: classical optimizer for QAOA parameters not specified; classical dynamic programming PBS solver discussed only as baseline in appendix
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PBS tree encoding and SymPy polynomial generation for cost operator
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure bitstrings, compute classical cost function, and evaluate success probability P0.1 / aggregated cost probabilities

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: probability amplification over layers; no explicit loss curve reported

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M·N^{m+1}) for the classical dynamic programming PBS solver; for special cases: star tree O(N^M), chain O(M·N^2), binary tree O(M·N^3)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Algorithm requires M·N logical qubits and O(p·M^2·N) gates; no resource estimate for fault‑tolerant implementation or advantage-scale instance is provided.

experiments.description: Gradient variance experiment studying barren plateau mitigation for the constrained-QAOA ansatz across increasing problem sizes.
key_results: Gradient variance estimated using finite-difference gradients with 100 samples.
Problem sizes tested correspond to 12, 16, 20, and 24 qubits (Table 1).
Log-variance plot (Figure 4) shows slower decay compared with typical barren plateau behavior reported in literature.
